decision: Use VTI (Vanguard Morningstar Total Stock Market ETF; 0.03%; 3531 holdings; 1-yr tracking difference 0.00pp; top-10 33.4%) as the US core.
alternatives_considered: VOO/IVV (S&P 500; 0.03%; top-10 37.9%); ITOT (S&P Total Market; 0.03%; 2437 holdings; spread 0.01%); SCHB (0.03%; 2381); SPYM ex-SPLG (0.02%; S&P 500)
evidence: Vanguard factsheets 30-Jun-2026; iShares/Schwab/SSGA pages 4-Sep-2026; S&P 500 ≈ 88% of total-market cap (IVV/ITOT 497K 31-Jul-2026)
counterargument: SPYM is 1bp cheaper and ITOT has a tighter published spread (0.01% vs VTI NOT FOUND); VOO outperformed VTI over 5-10 yrs. Mandate prefers total-market breadth; 1bp and the small/mid tilt are immaterial relative to the 30% withholding drag (~0.3%/yr) that all US-domiciled options share.
expected_outcome: Market return of US equities less ~0.03% ER and ~0.3% withholding drag
risk: US estate-tax exposure (pending policy decision 1); ticker/name change risk (VTI renamed 29-Jul-2026 — no methodology change)

decision: Split the Saudi core 50/50 between 9412 Albilad MSCI Saudi Equity ETF (0.35% all-in cap; ~250 holdings; AUM SAR 302m; PIF anchor; listed Oct-2025) and 9413 Al Rajhi MSCI Saudi Equity ETF (0.25% mgmt fee; ~250 holdings; AUM ~SAR 100m; listed 10-Aug-2026).
alternatives_considered: 9400 Yaqeen Saudi Equity ETF (30 stocks; 0.50%; AUM SAR 41m; persistent discount); 9402 SAB Invest Quant ETF (active quant; 0.75%); 9408 Albilad Growth (SMID; 0.55%); KSA US-listed (0.75% ER; 109 holdings; liquid; but US-situs + 30% withholding on ~2.8% yield ≈ 0.84%/yr); single-fund choice
evidence: Saudi Exchange ETF market watch 8-Sep-2026 14:35; Argaam; fund T&Cs; 9412 latest-session turnover SAR 29k vs a SAR 40k order; 9413 traded 174k units on 8-Sep
counterargument: Rule 3 (simplicity) argues for one fund. Rejected because a single SAR 40k order exceeds 9412's observed daily turnover; splitting halves order size per fund and diversifies new-fund/market-maker risk. Both funds are Shariah-screened (no conventional banks) — an unrequested tilt; KSA avoids the screen but costs ~1.6%/yr more and adds US-situs exposure.
expected_outcome: Broad Saudi equity return (Islamic index) less ~0.30% fees and ~0.5% entry slippage
risk: Thin liquidity; tracking error vs TASI from bank exclusion; 9413 has <1 month of trading history

decision: Use SGOV (iShares 0-3 Month Treasury Bond ETF; 0.09%; SEC yield 3.63% at 3-Sep; duration 0.10y; spread 0.01%; AUM $107bn) as the defensive & liquid sleeve.
alternatives_considered: BIL (0.1353%); USFR (0.15%; floating); SHV (0.15%; 0.26y); VBIL (0.06%; yield/spread NOT FOUND); 9404 Alinma Saudi Government Sukuk ETF (SAR; 0.25%; 0-5y duration; YTD -0.38%; turnover ~SAR 76k/day); 9403 Albilad Sovereign Sukuk ETF (YTD -2.35%; AUM SAR 56m); SAR money-market funds (e.g. Alinma SAR Liquidity Fund TER 0.14%; AUM SAR 6.3bn) — Sahm access unverified
evidence: Provider pages 4-Sep-2026; Saudi Exchange 8-Sep-2026; US Treasury 3-mo bill 3.91% (4-Sep)
counterargument: A SAR money-market fund is the purer Bogle choice (no FX; no withholding; no duration) if accessible. SGOV chosen because it is verifiably tradable via Sahm's US access; principal-stable; deeply liquid; SAR peg makes USD risk a tail (peg) risk rather than volatility. Conservative 30% withholding assumed on its ~3.6% yield (≈1.1%/yr drag) although QII designation may exempt it — to be verified. 9404 rejected as not cash-like (duration) and thin.
expected_outcome: ~2.5% net nominal yield (worst case) with ~zero principal volatility
risk: Peg break (tail); withholding applied by custodian; FX round-trip cost (~0.5%) if later redeployed to SAR

decision: Issue all initial core paper orders now (T0001-T0012) with next-open fills rather than waiting for the 11-Sep CPI or 16-Sep FOMC or for the Jazan attacks/Hormuz situation to resolve.
alternatives_considered: Delay 1-2 weeks; stagger US entry; use limit orders below the market
evidence: Mandate Rule 1: core entry is an execution decision not a timing decision; Portfolio C already provides the phased comparison
counterargument: Waiting into known event risk could avoid a drawdown — but that is market timing by another name; the mandate explicitly forbids it for the core. Saudi fills use a 0.5% slippage assumption and a +3% max-price guard to reflect thin books.
expected_outcome: Fills at 8-Sep (US) and 9-Sep (Saudi) opens; ~SAR 400-500 of estimated costs per full deployment
risk: Adverse open gap; unverifiable open price -> order stays PENDING

evidence: Investor instruction 2026-09-08 ~15:00 +03; no Saudi order had filled (Saudi market closed 15:00; orders were for the 9-Sep open); US open (09:30 ET = 16:30 +03) had not occurred at amendment time

risk: US concentration; estate-tax exposure now applies to ~90% of assets
